title: ansible.credentialtype Facet
description: The OBSERVED definition of an AWX/AAP credential TYPE — the schema a credential is an instance of — projected read-only by the ansible-automation Connector's controller half (§1.2, AWX-012). An observed foreign object, never a Stratt Named Kind. `managed: false` is the interesting value and the reason this namespace exists: AWX ships the built-in types (ssh, vault, aws…), but a CUSTOM type is something an operator wrote, and a credential of a custom type has no equivalent on the other side of a cutover until that type's fields and injectors exist there. Projecting it turns 'will my custom credential types survive?' from an unknown into an enumerable list. FIELD NAMES AND DELIVERY MODES, never values — but note this is a WEAKER §2.5 statement than the ones elsewhere in this Connector, and the difference is worth being precise about: a credential type holds no material BY CONSTRUCTION, because it is a schema; the material lives on credential INSTANCES, which ADR-0128 D2 already refuses to read (name and kind only). What is projected here is what the type ASKS FOR (`fields`, and which of them it marks `secret`) and HOW it delivers them (`injectorModes`: env | extra_vars | file), which is exactly what has to be reproduced. Injector TEMPLATES are deliberately not projected: a template names a field rather than carrying one (`{{ password }}`), so it is not a §2.5 risk, but it is arbitrary operator text that the delivery mode already summarises for every question a migration asks. Closed (§9).

kind.description: AWX's category: ssh | vault | net | scm | cloud | kubernetes | …

managed.description: a type AWX ships. FALSE is the migration-relevant value — a custom type exists nowhere else.

fields.description: the input field NAMES the type declares, sorted

secretFields.description: which of those fields the type marks secret — the ones that must arrive as a brokered CredentialRef on the other side (§2.5)

injectorModes.description: HOW the type delivers its fields to a job. The templates themselves are not projected — the mode answers every question a migration asks, and the template is arbitrary operator text.
